deferred_source_units.reason: The title's morning-help designation is preserved; it does not establish a particular episode or a sufficiently specific independent connection.
God's dwelling among holy ones and the praise of Israel are retained without identifying a particular heavenly assembly or earthly sanctuary.
The encircling calves and fat bulls are not identified with named historical attackers; a shared animal name would be insufficient.
Counting and being watched in one's bones do not establish John's separate not-broken-bone fulfillment; that proposed target remains uncredited.
Receiving blessing and mercy follows the ethical entrance conditions; no sufficiently specific independent target beyond a general reward-for-righteousness theme is retained.
The Lord of powers is explicitly the King of glory, but an exact counterpart beyond general divine-kingship titles has not been established for this unit.
The guidance and teaching of the meek are preserved; promises of land to the meek do not by themselves establish this different instructional relationship.
The joined appeal to see humiliation and toil and forgive all sins has not been given an independent target on the strength of generic forgiveness language alone.
The innocent and upright clinging to the speaker do not identify particular companions; generic fellowship among the virtuous is insufficient here.
Mercy before the eyes and conduct pleasing in truth are preserved; no particular act or independent textual counterpart has been established.
Hearing praise and recounting wonders remain this worshiping purpose; a general command to praise or recount God's deeds is insufficient for a retained pair.
Walking in innocence and asking redemption and mercy are preserved without treating every innocence or redemption prayer as a specific counterpart.
The flesh-devouring attackers' collapse is not identified with a particular military or Passion episode; that identity requires more than approaching enemies falling.
The lifted head and sacrifice of shouting in the tent do not establish a particular triumphal sacrifice elsewhere.
The cry for hearing and mercy has no sufficiently particular independent link retained beyond a general prayer formula.
The heart's hope, help and flesh blossoming anew are preserved without equating the bodily image with a specific healing or resurrection narrative.
The text says Lebanon, the calf and the beloved like a young one-horned animal; it does not explicitly name Hermon or Sanior, and that geographic identification remains uncredited.
The voice cleaving a flame of fire is not silently rewritten as lightning; no sufficiently precise independent counterpart has been retained.
Making deer ready does not expressly state childbirth in the supplied wording; the proposed birth-pain comparison remains uncredited, and general temple praise supplies no separate retained link.
The Davidic title names dedication of the house without identifying the house or occasion; Solomon's later dedication is not assigned as its event.
The future cry and petition do not establish an independent specific relationship beyond the general act of prayer.
Perpetual thanksgiving and freedom from grief remain this conclusion; a generic perpetual-praise verse is not retained as a specific counterpart.
The title of alarm is not assigned to a particular event in David's life without textual identification.
The declaration of hope and Thou art my God is preserved without making every profession of trust an independent cross-reference.
The contrasting pleas about shame and Hades do not identify a particular enemy's fate; general punishment language is insufficient for a retained link.
Concealed kindness prepared for those fearing and hoping is not identified with a particular promised treasure or later revelation.
The enclosed city is unnamed; the proposed identification with Keilah is not established and receives no credit.
Love for the Lord and His repayment of abundant arrogance are not attached to a specific arrogant ruler or incident.
The refuge and redemption from surrounding affliction do not identify a particular siege or escape; generic rescue imagery alone is not retained.
Rejoicing in God and hoping in His holy name remain the communal response; no independent match more specific than those general themes is retained.
The closing appeal for mercy according to hope is not given a target on the basis of mercy and hope alone.
